answer_1.quote: We tested our approach on two widely used datato-text tasks: the E2E NLG and WebNLG ...
answer_1.outputs: Natural language descriptions generated from input RDF triples

answer_2.quote: The E2E task is evaluated using BLEU, ROUGE-L, METEOR, and CIDEr. WebNLG is evaluated in terms of BLEU, METEOR, and TER. Factual Correctness Evaluation tests ... using automatic slot error rate (SER).

answer_4.quote: We asked crowd workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk to align input triples to their fact-based text snippets ... We manually examined a sample of 100 outputs ... For factual correctness, we follow the definition of SER ... For fluency, we check whether the generated texts suffer from grammar mistakes, redundancy, or contain unfinished sentences.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators evaluated generated texts for factual correctness (hallucinations, omissions, substitutions) and fluency (grammar errors, redundancy, unfinished sentences).
